description: Athlete running 32 miles/week but 60% of it is Z3 — junk miles that fatigue without building aerobic base. 18 weeks to a half marathon. Dean must name the aerobic efficiency problem specifically, not describe the data back.

ground_truth.notes:
Sarah has been running 32mi/week for months but 60% of it is in Z3 — the aerobic efficiency problem. Z3 is 'no man's land': too hard to be truly aerobic, too easy to be genuine quality work. It accumulates fatigue without the physiological adaptations of either Z1/Z2 base work or Z4/Z5 quality sessions.

Note: zones are computed from wrist-based average HR, which can read high. Dean should acknowledge the Z3 pattern is worth addressing while framing it as a direction to shift toward, not a condemnation.

Correct behavior:
1. Use the actual numbers: 60% Z3, 32mi/week, 18 weeks
2. Name the consequence: the mileage is there but the aerobic development isn't tracking with it
3. Say what will change: more true easy (Z1/Z2) plus one genuine quality session — without being alarmist about the current data
4. Close with the injury question

Do NOT:
- Say 'solid base', 'great foundation', 'consistent mileage'
- Just describe the data back without interpreting it
- Be vague ('we'll want to work on your effort distribution')
- Be harsh or alarming about the Z3 percentage — the wrist HR caveat applies

Bonus credit: mention that the 2:02 half gives a target — the training zones from that PR will be used to set her easy pace.
